Story & Plot

Medical courier Bryan unwittingly finds himself fighting for survival during one fateful, horrifying night as chaos collapses around him. Directed by Zach Cregger, the film drops its protagonists into a relentless survival horror experience filled with dwindling supplies and increasingly impossible goals. It brings a lively sense of gameplay and tense excitement that captures the foundational appeal of the survival-game experience.

Comedy & Entertainment

The movie balances its intense horror elements with unexpected laughs, camp, hijinks, and unhinged humor. Reviewers note that this mixture of horror and comedy counteracts the stakes while providing a genuinely fun, fast-paced thrill to watch with a crowd. It delivers a fast-paced and entertaining ride without relying on specific scripted sketches.

Performances & Direction

The cast features Austin Abrams, Paul Walter Hauser, Kali Reis, Zach Cherry, and Johnno Wilson. Austin Abrams leads the ensemble with a strong central performance that anchors the terrifying events of the night. The wider cast helps drive the survival-focused narrative forward with engaging energy.

Strengths

  • laser focus on survival horror
  • strong central performance by Austin Abrams
  • effective blend of tension and laughs
  • relentless pacing
  • faithful game-like structure

Weaknesses

While the film is a blast and delivers plenty of excitement, the mixture of horror and comedy can sometimes counteract the serious stakes of the survival plot. Additionally, some viewers might find that the premise leans heavily into familiar video game tropes and arcade-like limitations.

Final verdict

Resident Evil succeeds as a simple, exciting, and scary live-action video game adaptation directed by Zach Cregger. It provides a relentless good time that works well for both longtime fans and newcomers alike. Recommended for anyone looking for a fast-paced theatrical horror thrill ride.
